name: @media-router/plugin-transcoder
description: Video transcoder — one MPEG-TS video input fanned out to N re-encoded quality renditions (ABR ladder)

mediaRouter.description: Decodes one muxed/mpegts video stream once and re-encodes it into several quality renditions — set width, height and bitrate per output, each on its own MPEG-TS port. Input must be H.264 (the decoder is a fixed h264parse ! avdec_h264); the OUTPUT codec is configurable (H.264/H.265/AV1). Feeding an H.265 source produces no video.

renditions.description: Output quality renditions — "+ Add" creates another MPEG-TS output port. Each is decoded once and re-encoded at the given size and bitrate.

codec.description: Override output codec for this rendition. Blank = inherit the global codec.

encoderImpl.description: Override encoder implementation for this rendition. Resolved against this rendition's codec. Blank = inherit the global implementation.

rateControl.description: Override rate control for this rendition. Blank = inherit.

speedPreset.description: Override speed↔quality preset for this rendition (software x264/x265 / VA-API only). Raise it on just the top rendition for cleaner motion without paying the CPU on every quality. Blank = inherit.

h264Profile.description: Override H.264 profile for this rendition (H.264 only) — e.g. Baseline on a low rendition targeting old decoders. Blank = inherit.

sceneCut.description: Override scene-cut threshold for this rendition (software x264/x265 only; 0 = off). Blank = inherit.

codec.description: Output video codec (applied to every rendition)

rateControl.description: Encoder rate control for every rendition. CBR (default) holds a constant bitrate (peak = target) — best for fixed-bandwidth UDP/SRT/MPEG-TS, since bursts can overrun the receiver's buffer and read as packet loss. VBR targets the bitrate as an average and lets per-frame size vary for better quality on motion, with the peak capped at 1.5x to bound bursts.

encoderImpl.description: Encoder implementation. Auto prefers a hardware block, then software. V4L2 is the Pi's SoC encoder; VA-API is the Intel iGPU (x86) — the only H.265 encoder on Intel boxes with no x265enc, and it offloads the CPU. Software (x264/x265) exposes the richest tuning (scene-cut, profiles) and runs many renditions at once. The dropdown only lists impls actually installed for the chosen codec.

speedPreset.description: Software x264/x265 speed↔quality preset (on Intel VA-API it maps to target-usage; ignored by V4L2 hardware and AV1). Faster presets use less CPU but block up on hard content — fast motion and fine/scrolling text; slower presets spend more CPU for cleaner quality at the same bitrate. Default 'ultrafast' suits a CPU-bound Pi; on a box with spare cores raise it (e.g. Fast/Medium) for cleaner motion. Applies to every rendition and rebuilds the pipeline.

h264Profile.description: H.264 output profile — constrains encoder features for decoder compatibility (H.264 only; ignored for H.265/AV1). Baseline is the most widely decodable (no CABAC or B-frames — best for old/embedded hardware decoders); Main adds CABAC; High adds the 8×8 transform for best efficiency. Auto lets the encoder choose. Applies to every rendition and rebuilds the pipeline.

sceneCut.description: Scene-cut detection threshold for software x264/x265 (H.264/H.265 only; ignored by V4L2 and VA-API hardware). When the encoder detects a hard cut it inserts an adaptive keyframe there, so the picture snaps clean at the cut instead of blocking until the next scheduled keyframe. 40 is x264's default; higher = more sensitive (more keyframes, more bitrate); 0 = off (strict fixed-GOP — use for byte-aligned ABR renditions). Note: tune=zerolatency runs with no lookahead, so detection is reactive rather than optimally placed. Applies to every rendition and rebuilds the pipeline.

framerate.description: Output framerate (shared by all renditions, keeps keyframes aligned for ABR)

deinterlace.description: Interlaced sources (1080i etc.) are deinterlaced automatically by default — progressive sources pass through untouched. 'Keep interlaced' skips deinterlacing and passes the fields through; only useful when renditions keep the source resolution (scaling interlaced fields corrupts them). Note: only the software (x264) H.264 encoder can flag its output as interlaced; VA-API/V4L2 outputs remain progressive-flagged.

gopFrames.description: Keyframe interval in frames (the standard encoder unit — x264/x265 key-int-max). A keyframe is forced every N frames; shorter = faster channel-join/recovery but more bitrate. At 50 fps, 50 = 1 s, 100 = 2 s.

cpuDecodeThreading.description: Software decode threading. MULTI-CORE (default) forces FFmpeg frame threading (thread-type=frame) so the decode spreads across all CPU cores instead of pinning one at 100% — important on the Pi 5, which has no hardware H.264 decoder. Costs ~1 frame of latency per core. SINGLE CORE is GStreamer's default live behaviour (one core, lowest latency) — use if latency matters more than spreading the load.

bufferMs.description: Buffer (ms) — sizes the network jitter queue and the decoded-frame buffer that lets the decoder work ahead. Absorbs timing jitter so a momentary stall drops fewer frames (less macroblocking). It does NOT add decode cores. 200 ms is a sane default; lower it for tighter latency, raise it if you still see drops. Costs this much latency.
